title: Session 2: Naming of Club and Launch Campaign

slides.title: Welcome to the Nagarika Club!
slides.tip: Play welcome music. Make sure all children are seated.

slides.title: Club Naming & Launch Campaign
slides.tip: Introduce today's session title. Display title in center of screen.

slides.title: Welcome to another session!
body: Quick check — is everyone sitting in their groups?
Today let's give our club a name…
slides.tip: Re-check group formation. Confirm everyone is in their group.

slides.title: Name your Club!
body: What name would you like to give your club?
Think about the club's purpose, think creatively about active citizenship, and suggest inspiring, effective names.
slides.tip: Write students' suggestions on the blackboard.

slides.title: What's your club name?
body: One person, one name, one vote.
Choose wisely. Be fair.
The name with the most votes becomes your club name!
slides.tip: Raise hands for each name and count. Write results on the board.

slides.title: Time to vote!
body: Raise hands for each name and count the votes.
slides.tip: Conduct the vote. Each child gets only one vote.

slides.title: And… your club name is…?
body: ______________ Nagarika Club….
Remember, the power to bring change lies within you!
slides.tip: Drum roll and applause. Ask children to clap.

slides.title: Be active citizens!
body: You don't have to be grown up to be an active citizen! Even as children, you can be active citizens!
In previous years, hundreds of club children have become Change Champions and done amazing Ripples of Change.
But with power comes responsibility.
slides.tip: Show the image of change-makers of all ages.

slides.title: Committee formation
body: Let's now select our class leader and the core committee for the club.
Today we will see democracy in action!
slides.tip: Introduce the process of forming a committee through democracy.

slides.title: India's election process
body: Do you know how we choose our leaders in India?
Do you know the different levels of government where elections are held?
slides.tip: Give children time to guess. Explain Gram Panchayat, State, Centre levels.

slides.title: What qualities should an ideal representative have?
slides.tip: Give children time to answer. Then proceed to the video questions.

items.question: What qualities should an ideal representative have?
If your friend and another student are candidates, who do you vote for?
Does it matter if they are a boy or a girl?
How would you feel if your friends didn't vote for you? What if you lost?

kn_script: ಚುನಾವಣೆಗೆ ಹೋಗುವ ಮೊದಲು, ಒಬ್ಬ ಆದರ್ಶ ಪ್ರತಿನಿಧಿಗೆ ಇರಬೇಕಾದ ಗುಣಗಳೇನು?
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸ್ನೇಹಿತ ಮತ್ತು ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬ ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿ ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿಗಳಾಗಿದ್ದರೆ, ನೀವು ಯಾರಿಗೆ ಮತ ಹಾಕುತ್ತೀರಿ?
ಆ ಕೆಲಸವನ್ನು ಮಾಡುವವರು ಹುಡುಗ ಅಥವಾ ಹುಡುಗಿ ಎಂಬುದು ಮುಖ್ಯವಾಗುತ್ತದೆಯೇ?
ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸ್ನೇಹಿತರೇ ನಿಮಗೆ ಮತ ಹಾಕದಿದ್ದರೆ ನಿಮಗೆ ಹೇಗನ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ?
ಒಂದು ವೇಳೆ ನೀವು ಚುನಾವಣೆಗೆ ನಿಂತು ಸೋತರೆ?
slides.transcript: Before we vote — what qualities should an ideal representative have? If your friend and another student are candidates, and the other student is better at the job, who do you vote for? Does it matter if they are a boy or a girl? How would you feel if your friends did not vote for you? What if you ran and lost — how would you view the winner?
slides.tip: Allow discussion time after each question. Press Next Question to advance.

slides.title: Let's prepare our committee!
body: Steps to follow:
Your first step is to choose one person from your group to be part of the Core Committee.
You have 2 minutes!
slides.tip: 2 minute timer needed. Reminder sound at 1 minute.

slides.title: Elected members come forward
body: Well done! All elected members, come to the front of the class.
Who would like to stand as Club President? Come forward.
You have time to tell us why the Club should elect you.
slides.tip: Give each candidate 30 seconds to speak.

slides.title: Affirmative Action
body: If one gender has very few or no representatives:
Has the under-represented group received justice?
How can their voice or opinions be heard?
How can we ensure boys and girls both get a fair chance?
slides.tip: Introduce Reservation or Affirmative Action. Explain the importance of gender equality in the committee.

slides.title: Let's vote!
body: Who will be our club president?
You have 1 vote.
slides.tip: Have candidates stand at the back. Ask remaining children to close their eyes. Count votes for each candidate.

slides.title: Congratulations!
body: Congratulations to our president and core committee!
Now it's time for all of us to work together!
slides.tip: If it gets noisy, use the calmers from Session 1.

slides.title: I Am The Change
body: Club Launch Campaign
slides.tip: Show campaign examples. Introduce the club launch campaign.

slides.title: Committee's responsibility
body: Give the responsibility of the launch campaign's success to the club committee.
slides.tip: Distribute annexures to groups and encourage them to take the lead on the launch.

slides.title: Thank You
slides.tip: Thank the children. End of session.
